quick.summary: How to build pipelines that let you restart without starting over.
quick.takeaway: Save progress at clear steps so you can fix failures without redoing everything.

beats.line: My process failed at the last step. Why did I have to restart everything?
Think of a video game without save points.
Dying means you go all the way back to level one.
Exactly. A good data flow saves progress at clear stages.
If a step breaks, you only fix that step and resume.
Can I just say safe to repeat?
Safe to repeat is exactly right.
So I save data after big steps. If it breaks, I restart there.
You will never play from level one again.

quiz.question: What is the benefit of making pipeline steps safe to repeat?
options: You can restart from the point of failure instead of the very beginning.
It automatically writes the data twice just to be certain.
It speeds up the process so it finishes in half the time.
It guarantees that the code will never break.
quiz.explanation: When steps are safe to repeat, they act like checkpoints. You only rerun what failed.

quiz.question: A good pipeline should always wipe all data and start from scratch if an error occurs.
quiz.explanation: Starting from scratch wastes time and resources. You should save progress at clear stages.
